'Human composting' bill promises a new way to be buried
Evidence: stated bill, actual process, stated intent
#Sustainability #EndofLife

An independent MP plans to introduce a bill for 'human composting' (natural organic reduction) in NSW, offering a sustainable alternative to burial and cremation. Premier Minns finds it 'a bit weird'.

The process involves placing a body with organic materials to break down into soil for planting. It's legal in 14 US states and Germany, with advocates citing environmental benefits.

The article discusses a proposed bill in New South Wales that would legalize 'human composting,' a process where human remains are transformed into soil. This is presented as an environmentally friendly alternative to burial and cremation.

The Bright Side:
This initiative offers a more sustainable and potentially cost-effective end-of-life option, allowing individuals to contribute positively to the environment even after death.
